clue.text: Where drinks go to the right place?

definitions.text: Where drinks go to the right place?

parts.words: Where drinks go to the right place?
parts.note: read as a city name split in two: glasses of a fortified wine (plural) heading for the opening in the face where they belong; the city is a naval port on England's south coast

explanation.surface: A question about the proper destination for drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer: PORTS, the fortified wines, go to the MOUTH, the right place for them. PORTSMOUTH is a naval city on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a city name that splits into drinks plus the body part that takes them in.

clue.text: A spread of the head

definitions.meaning: a smooth meat or fish paste spread on toast
an old word for the crown of the head

explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a savoury paste for spreading, and pate is an archaic word for the skull or crown.

clue.text: Titaness the ambassador found ip Burlington House

indicators.note: found (in) says where the ambassador is located, so his letters sit inside the institution's

parts.note: Burlington House in London is home of the Royal Academy, RA
an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, HE

explanation.surface: A mythological goddess bumps into an envoy at a London art institution.
explanation.walkthrough: The print reads 'ip' for 'in'. Burlington House on London's Piccadilly is the home of the Royal Academy of Arts; an ambassador is styled His Excellency.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Rhea is one of the Titans, mother of Zeus.

clue.text: Odd pieces of money

indicators.note: odd here means strange or irregular, telling us the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A remark about stray coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' signals rearranging PIECES.
explanation.definitionFit: Specie is coin money, as opposed to paper notes.

clue.text: Methodical N C O keeping others in their place?

definitions.text: Methodical N C O keeping others in their place?

parts.words: Methodical N C O keeping others in their place?
parts.note: a tidy non-commissioned officer who keeps everyone in line; the title is that of an army sergeant on daily duty

explanation.surface: A neat-minded army NCO who keeps the ranks in order.
explanation.walkthrough: Methodical gives ORDERLY, and an NCO keeping others in their place is a SERGEANT; together they name the real duty rank.
explanation.definitionFit: An orderly sergeant is the sergeant detailed for the day's duties in a unit, a non-commissioned officer.

clue.text: Given out wrongly can get the bird

indicators.note: wrongly given out means the letters of the word out are dealt in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Something handed out in error lets you obtain a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given out wrongly' scrambles OUT into TOU; add CAN as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical bird with a huge colourful bill.

clue.text: Dash about for fish

indicators.note: about here means turned around or rearranged, applied to the word just before it

explanation.surface: Someone rushes around looking for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges DASH.
explanation.definitionFit: The shad is a herring-like fish that swims upriver to spawn.

clue.text: Manicurist in olden times?

parts.note: a young woman who tends hands, put in the language of old-fashioned stories for a female servant

explanation.surface: A question about who did nails in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as HAND MAIDEN: a maid for hands, a manicurist; a handmaiden is an old word for a female attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: Handmaiden is an archaic term for a personal maidservant, and split up it suggests a girl tending hands.

clue.text: Showing Pluto to be an instrumentalist?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman name for Pluto, god of the underworld
an instrumentalist is someone performing on an instrument, i.e. playing

explanation.surface: Proof that the planet or the cartoon dog is a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto is the god of the underworld, also called Dis, not the dwarf planet or Disney's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Displaying means exhibiting, putting on view.

clue.text: Turned some out. Great!

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: Some people were turned away, and someone cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder: TURNED SOME, scrambled ('out'), gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous as an exclamation of approval means splendid or excellent.

clue.text: The burden on America

parts.note: taken as written
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A statement that the weight falls on the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a responsibility or obligation that weighs on someone.

clue.text: Sing a carol for a change with the woodwind

indicators.note: changing the letters of the carol-singing phrase means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Singers try a carol with woodwind accompaniment for variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges SING A CAROL.
explanation.definitionFit: The cor anglais is a woodwind instrument, a tenor oboe.

clue.text: America's after this record Greek coin thrower

indicators.note: after this means the American letters follow the record and coin

parts.note: a gramophone record is a disc
the obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: The USA follows a Greek coin and a record in some ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' tempts as a sporting best, but it is a gramophone disc. Discobolus is Myron's famous Greek statue of a discus thrower.
explanation.definitionFit: Discobolus is Greek for a discus thrower, as in Myron's statue.

clue.text: Heights to which artists finally rise, maybe, in Spain

indicators.note: finally says the artists come at the end of the answer
maybe here suggests a possible version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, artists

explanation.surface: Painters ultimately climb Spanish mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise, maybe' scrambles RISE into SIER; 'artists finally' puts RAS last. 'in Spain' tells you the heights are Spanish mountain ranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierras are jagged mountain ranges, the word being Spanish for a saw.

clue.text: Boy about to joust? Cheese it!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the boy goes around the jousting word

parts.note: a boy is a son
to tilt is to joust with a lance

explanation.surface: A lad is about to joust and is told to scram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese it!' is old slang for 'clear off!', a misleading command; the definition is just 'Cheese'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a blue English cheese.

clue.text: Took comfort being thus tied up

parts.note: thus means so
laced means tied up, as with shoelaces

explanation.surface: Someone found consolation while being tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Solaced means comforted, consoled in distress.

clue.text: Drug I take in down with nothing added at first

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Drug I take in down with nothing added at first' lacks the figure of a cross-reference: the wordplay needs 'in 1 down' (PATE, with I inside, after O), and the check cannot accept the dropped '1' as an OCR repair
annotationWithheld.clue: Drug I take in down with nothing added at first

clue.text: Bellini's heroine lake as usual

parts.note: Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: The opera's heroine is behind schedule, as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellini's 1831 opera Norma gives NORMA; L is the abbreviation for lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual, ordinary.

clue.text: Icy comment warming us to Faith and Hope?

definitions.text: Icy comment warming us to Faith and Hope?

parts.words: Icy comment warming us to Faith and Hope?
parts.note: a frosty simile, recalling that faith and hope are paired with a third virtue in St Paul's list, which is cold in this saying

explanation.surface: A chilly remark that nevertheless makes us fonder of two virtues.
explanation.walkthrough: Faith, hope and charity are the three virtues of 1 Corinthians 13; 'as cold as charity' is a simile for icy, so the third virtue makes the other two look warm by comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile is a set phrase meaning extremely cold or unfeeling.

clue.text: Rock starter and good French historian

indicators.note: the Rock is the starter, so its letters go first

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, often shortened to Gib
bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A rock music opener and a fine French writer of history.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rock is Gibraltar, 'Gib'. Edward Gibbon wrote The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Gibbon was the eighteenth-century English historian of Rome's decline.

clue.text: Ornamental work Lionel fashioned

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the name's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man named Lionel crafted decorative work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' rearranges LIONEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic inlay used to decorate engraved silver.

clue.text: Humble cleric taking me to heart

indicators.note: taking means the cleric holds the other word inside him
to heart says the word goes into the middle

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: A modest clergyman takes something personally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking me to heart' puts ME into the middle of DEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean is to lower or degrade, i.e. to humble someone.

clue.text: Arid retreat for a poet

parts.note: arid means dry
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A dry hideaway for a writer of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dryden was the seventeenth-century English poet laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a Restoration poet and dramatist.

clue.text: Poor grading for one so hard-fisted

indicators.note: poor here means badly done, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: A stingy person gives bad marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges GRADING.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a miser, someone tight-fisted with money.

clue.text: Done in a notably efficient way

definitions.text: Done in a notably efficient way

indicators.note: in tells us the word sits within the next word's letters

explanation.surface: A job carried out with notable efficiency.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in plain sight inside 'notably', and the whole clue describes something done skilfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Ably means competently, in a capable manner.

clue.text: Storage tower accommodating crude oils

indicators.note: crude means rough or unrefined, so the letters of the word are in a rough order

explanation.surface: A tower is holding unrefined petroleum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' looks like it describes the oil, but it rearranges OILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tall tower for storing grain or other bulk material.

clue.text: Puts on address engineers vacated

indicators.note: vacated means the engineers leave the word, so their letters are taken out

parts.note: REs are Royal Engineers, the army's engineering corps

explanation.surface: Someone gives a speech after the engineers have left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineers vacated' removes R, E and S from ADDRESS, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to put on extra, to append.

clue.text: Suitable beverage for retired gentlefolk?

parts.note: a pub drink mixing two beers, named as if it described elderly gentle people

explanation.surface: A question about what pensioners should drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Old and mild is a British pub mix of old ale and mild ale; read literally it describes aged, gentle folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink's name doubles as a description of elderly, gentle people.

clue.text: Point has shifted, and it's a bind

parts.note: S is south, a compass point

indicators.note: shifted means moved around, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A point has moved, and it is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bind' looks like 'a nuisance' but means something tied round; the compass point is south.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth tied round the waist, something that binds.

clue.text: Ominous the canvas cover lets water all round

indicators.note: the leaky word goes all round the canvas, holding it inside

parts.note: porous material lets water through
a tent is a canvas cover

explanation.surface: A threatening sign: the tent leaks everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lets water' reads as a verb phrase about the tent, but it defines a leaky material that surrounds the canvas cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Portentous means foreshadowing something bad, ominous.
